figures.alt: A single canvas with sixteen labeled casta panels, each showing a family of mixed ancestry with its category name.
figures.caption: Casta painting containing a complete set of 16 casta combinations (racial classifications in the Spanish colonies), 18th century, oil on canvas.

books.section: Topic 1.5 Labor, Slavery, and Caste in the Spanish Colonial System
The Social Structure of Spanish America
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

options.text: That classifying people by ancestry had become a systematic preoccupation.

options.misconception: Confuses the number of categories with the number of paintings owned.
options.text: That every colonial household owned exactly sixteen casta paintings.

options.misconception: Turns a display of categories into their abolition.
options.text: That the Spanish Crown had abolished all racial categories entirely.

options.misconception: Treats a cultural display as a legal document.
options.text: That casta paintings served as legal documents in colonial court cases.

rationales.A: A sixteen-panel catalog of ancestry combinations is not casual decoration, it is a system laid out for display. Producing such a complete visual taxonomy shows how deeply the ranking of people by descent had penetrated colonial culture.
rationales.B: The number sixteen reflects the categories, not household ownership. No evidence says every household owned such a set.
rationales.C: The set displays categories; it did not abolish them. A catalog of ranks is the opposite of abolition.
rationales.D: These were cultural objects displaying the hierarchy, not court records. They hung in homes, they did not decide cases.
rationales.general:
1. Look at the whole canvas. Sixteen panels, each with a labeled family, cover every ancestry combination.
2. Ask what a complete catalog means. It means classification had become a system, not a habit.
3. Ask what it does not mean. A display is not a census of households, an abolition, or a court record.
4. Name the pattern. Ranking by descent had become a preoccupation of colonial culture itself.
Remember: a complete catalog of categories shows a system at work; ask what the system was for.

stem: What does the existence of such a comprehensive set best indicate about Spanish colonial culture?

stimulus.source_note: Casta painting, 18th century, oil on canvas, public domain; Wikimedia Commons.
stimulus.text: This single canvas gathers sixteen casta paintings, each labeling a different combination of parents and child. The panels run from 'Español con India, Mestizo' to 'Noteentiendo con India, Tornaatras,' covering Spanish, Indigenous, African, and mixed ancestry in every combination.
